mathematical_review.reason: For a<=b, continuous g is interval integrable. EqOn on Ioo transfers integrability via congr_uIoo after uIoo_of_le and transfers the integral via integral_congr_Ioo_of_le. Lebesgue endpoints have zero measure; arbitrary f endpoint values and a=b cause no missing premise.

For a<b, Ioo(a,b) is a left neighborhood of b. Continuity of g gives its left limit g(b), and eventual equality transfers it to f. This is valid for arbitrary target topology, without Hausdorff or endpoint-agreement assumptions.

Induction includes the zero-arc base. In the successor step, castSucc restricts the first n arcs and last n gives the final arc. Monotonicity supplies ordered endpoints. IntervalIntegrable.trans and adjacent integral addition join the pieces; Fin.sum_univ_castSucc exactly splits the finite sum. Repeated partition points are allowed.

The adapter derives monotonicity of snoc(cons0 t,T) from Prefix strict ordering and all t_i<T, with only nonnegative T needed for the initial point. For s in each open arc, hgrid bounds0<=s<=T, hclipcoe removes the clamp, and hafter establishes that every later record is ineligible. It then consumes precisely the maximum-eligible-record path clause of accepted actual_finite_count_path_law. It does not assume open-arc agreement or an actual-path provider as a binder.

Imported actual harmonic-flow and bounce-rate theorems provide ordinary finite-dimensional phase continuity under the original six assumptions. Composition yields continuous fixed-state arc rates. finite_arc_integral supplies interval integrability and the finite arc integral sum. integral_comp_sub_right translates each arc to0 and coe_toNNReal uses nonnegative duration. Strict Prefix spacing selects the incoming arc for each left limit; composition with continuous rate gives the rate limit.

index_and_endpoint_review.grid: grid has n+2 entries [0,t1,...,tn,T]; j:Fin(n+1) indexes n+1 arcs. grid(j.castSucc)=a_j and grid(j.succ)=a_(j+1). Last arc is from t_n toT.
index_and_endpoint_review.incoming: i:Fin n selects event t_(i+1); i.castSucc selects z_i; i.castSucc.castSucc selects a_i. hnext uses succ_castSucc, snoc_castSucc and cons_succ to identify the following endpoint exactly with t.val i.
index_and_endpoint_review.n_zero: The actual proof invokes finite_arc_integral with one arc, from0 toT. No event left limits are demanded. The generic zero-arc case is also sound.
index_and_endpoint_review.T_zero: For n=0, both endpoints coincide and interval integrability and zero hazard identity hold. For n>0 Prefix is empty. No proof step incorrectly assumes T>0 globally.
index_and_endpoint_review.jump_endpoints: No equality with an incoming arc is demanded at an event; Gamma chooses the post-bounce state there. Finite-null endpoint changes justify the hazard integral, while a genuine left neighborhood gives the incoming phase/rate limit.
index_and_endpoint_review.terminal_endpoint: T enters the final integral endpoint. Open-arc agreement is sufficient and does not omit terminal survival time from the hazard sum.
index_and_endpoint_review.rank_zero_zero_rate: Neither the generic argument nor the adapters divide by a rate or assume nontrivial E. Continuous zero rates and singleton phase spaces are included. Zero-normal reflection remains the already fixed total Lean definition.
index_and_endpoint_review.coordinate_path_semantics: The same coordinate-product path carrier and pointwise interpolation from93 are used. No Skorokhod topology, continuous full path, measurable joint evaluation on the uncountable path carrier, or new path-space regularity premise appears. The only continuity is that of finite-dimensional flow/rate and each fixed arc.
index_and_endpoint_review.clock_cases: The conclusion is deterministic for prescribed positive ordered tuples. No AE quantifier change, actual finite-wait premise, raw zero-clock exclusion or new stochastic assumption is introduced.
